final_selections.research_reason: Team B's SoT conceded shows a pronounced venue split: away matches produce materially higher SoT conceded than home matches (evidence: shots_on_target against away_mean vs home_mean), well above the competition environment mean. This fixture places Team B in an AWAY role, directly invoking this vulnerability. The research question is whether Team B's away-specific SoT concession rate differs significantly from their overall baseline — structurally motivated by an observed and persistent home/away asymmetry across multiple corroborating defensive metrics (shots conceded, clearances, saves).
final_selections.mechanism_summary: When playing away, Team B appears less able to suppress opponent shot quality, possibly due to reduced territorial control (lower away clearances), opponent home crowd pressure, or a more reactive defensive posture. This venue-conditioned concession pattern is corroborated by the shots-conceded and clearances splits, making it a cross-metric consistent signal rather than noise in a single stat.
final_selections.why_simple_average_is_insufficient: The long-run baseline averages home and away exposures together, masking a structurally important venue asymmetry. Since Team B is always the AWAY team in this fixture, using the unconditional baseline would systematically underweight the away-specific concession rate that is actually relevant to this match-up.
final_selections.support_warning: The venue split in SoT conceded is large; if it reflects opponent quality differences rather than true venue effect, the conditioning may overfit. The shots and clearances splits corroborate direction but do not isolate the mechanism conclusively.
